# Form Integration

## Overview

FidoUI components are "headless-friendly" — they work with any form library. This guide covers **TanStack Form** and **React Hook Form**, both of which are used across the org. Each section includes setup, component-specific patterns, and error handling.

Because FidoUI components use a mix of native and custom APIs (some expose `onChange`, others use `onValueChange` or `onCheckedChange`), the key to a smooth integration is understanding which prop maps to which form library callback.

## TanStack Form + Zod

### Setup

```tsx
import { useForm } from '@tanstack/react-form'
import { z } from 'zod'

import { Input } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/input'
import { Field } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/field'
import { Textarea } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/textarea'
import { Select, SelectItem } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/select'
import { DatePicker } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/date-picker'
import { Checkbox } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/checkbox'
import { RadioGroup, RadioItem } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/radio-group'
```

### Error Handling Helper

Since TanStack Form stores errors as arrays, use a small helper to extract a displayable string:

```tsx
function getFieldError(field: { state: { meta: { isTouched: boolean; isValid: boolean; errors: unknown[] } } }) {
  if (!field.state.meta.isTouched || field.state.meta.isValid) return undefined;
  return field.state.meta.errors
    .map((e) => (typeof e === 'string' ? e : String(e)))
    .join(', ');
}
```

### Basic Pattern — Input

```tsx
const form = useForm({
  defaultValues: { email: '' },
  onSubmit: async ({ value }) => {
    console.log(value);
  },
});

// Inside your JSX:
<form.Field
  name="email"
  validators={{
    onBlur: z.string().email('Please enter a valid email'),
  }}
>
  {(field) => (
    <Field label="Email" error={getFieldError(field)}>
      <Input
        name={field.name}
        value={field.state.value}
        onChange={(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value)}
        onBlur={field.handleBlur}
      />
    </Field>
  )}
</form.Field>
```

### Textarea

```tsx
<form.Field
  name="bio"
  validators={{
    onBlur: z.string().max(500, 'Bio must be 500 characters or fewer'),
  }}
>
  {(field) => (
    <Textarea
      label="Bio"
      name={field.name}
      value={field.state.value}
      onChange={(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value)}
      onBlur={field.handleBlur}
      maxLength={500}
      error={getFieldError(field)}
    />
  )}
</form.Field>
```

### Select

Select uses `onValueChange` instead of `onChange`. Map accordingly. Label chrome
matches Field / Textarea — use `labelPlacement="stacked"` (default) or
`"internal"`, plus `optional`, `tooltip`, `hideLabel`, `description`, and
`error`.

```tsx
<form.Field
  name="country"
  validators={{
    onBlur: z.string().min(1, 'Please select a country'),
  }}
>
  {(field) => (
    <Select
      label="Country"
      labelPlacement="stacked"
      name={field.name}
      value={field.state.value}
      onValueChange={(value) => field.handleChange(value)}
      error={getFieldError(field)}
    >
      <SelectItem value="us">United States</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="ca">Canada</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="mx">Mexico</SelectItem>
    </Select>
  )}
</form.Field>
```

### DatePicker

DatePicker is controlled with a `Date | undefined` value. Close the popover to
mark the field touched when validation should run on blur. `dateFormat` controls
how the selected date is displayed.

```tsx
<form.Field
  name="moveInDate"
  validators={{
    onChange: z.date().optional(),
  }}
>
  {(field) => (
    <DatePicker
      label="Move-in date"
      optional
      dateFormat="MM/dd/yyyy"
      value={field.state.value}
      onChange={(value) => field.handleChange(value)}
      onOpenChange={(open) => {
        if (!open) field.handleBlur()
      }}
      error={getFieldError(field)}
    />
  )}
</form.Field>
```

### Checkbox

Checkbox uses `checked` / `onCheckedChange` instead of `value` / `onChange`:

```tsx
<form.Field
  name="terms"
  validators={{
    onBlur: z.literal(true, { errorMap: () => ({ message: 'You must accept the terms' }) }),
  }}
>
  {(field) => (
    <Checkbox
      label="I accept the terms and conditions"
      name={field.name}
      checked={field.state.value}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => field.handleChange(checked)}
      error={getFieldError(field)}
    />
  )}
</form.Field>
```

### RadioGroup

RadioGroup uses `onValueChange`, similar to Select:

```tsx
<form.Field
  name="plan"
  validators={{
    onBlur: z.enum(['free', 'pro', 'enterprise'], { message: 'Please select a plan' }),
  }}
>
  {(field) => (
    <RadioGroup
      label="Plan"
      name={field.name}
      value={field.state.value}
      onValueChange={(value) => field.handleChange(value)}
      error={getFieldError(field)}
    >
      <RadioItem value="free" label="Free" />
      <RadioItem value="pro" label="Pro" />
      <RadioItem value="enterprise" label="Enterprise" />
    </RadioGroup>
  )}
</form.Field>
```

## React Hook Form + Zod

### Setup

```tsx
import { useForm, Controller } from 'react-hook-form'
import { zodResolver } from '@hookform/resolvers/zod'
import { z } from 'zod'

import { Input } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/input'
import { Field } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/field'
import { Textarea } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/textarea'
import { Select, SelectItem } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/select'
import { DatePicker } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/date-picker'
import { Checkbox } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/checkbox'
import { RadioGroup, RadioItem } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/radio-group'

const schema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email(),
  bio: z.string().max(500).optional(),
  country: z.string().min(1, 'Required'),
  moveInDate: z.date().optional(),
  terms: z.literal(true, { errorMap: () => ({ message: 'You must accept the terms' }) }),
  plan: z.enum(['free', 'pro', 'enterprise']),
});

type FormValues = z.infer<typeof schema>;
```

### Pattern 1: register() for Native Elements

Input wraps a native `<input>`, so `register()` works directly on `Input`. Put labels and errors on `Field`:

```tsx
const { register, handleSubmit, formState: { errors } } = useForm<FormValues>({
  resolver: zodResolver(schema),
});

<Field label="Email" error={errors.email?.message}>
  <Input {...register('email')} />
</Field>

<Textarea
  label="Bio"
  {...register('bio')}
  maxLength={500}
  error={errors.bio?.message}
/>
```

### Pattern 2: Controller for Custom Components

Select, Checkbox, RadioGroup, and other custom components do not use native `onChange` — wrap them with `Controller`:

**Select:**

```tsx
<Controller
  name="country"
  control={control}
  render={({ field, fieldState }) => (
    <Select
      label="Country"
      value={field.value}
      onValueChange={field.onChange}
      onOpenChange={() => field.onBlur()}
      error={fieldState.error?.message}
    >
      <SelectItem value="us">United States</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="ca">Canada</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="mx">Mexico</SelectItem>
    </Select>
  )}
/>
```

**DatePicker:**

```tsx
<Controller
  name="moveInDate"
  control={control}
  render={({ field, fieldState }) => (
    <DatePicker
      label="Move-in date"
      optional
      dateFormat="MM/dd/yyyy"
      value={field.value}
      onChange={field.onChange}
      onOpenChange={(open) => {
        if (!open) field.onBlur()
      }}
      error={fieldState.error?.message}
    />
  )}
/>
```

**Checkbox:**

```tsx
<Controller
  name="terms"
  control={control}
  render={({ field, fieldState }) => (
    <Checkbox
      label="I accept the terms and conditions"
      checked={field.value}
      onCheckedChange={field.onChange}
      error={fieldState.error?.message}
    />
  )}
/>
```

**RadioGroup:**

```tsx
<Controller
  name="plan"
  control={control}
  render={({ field, fieldState }) => (
    <RadioGroup
      label="Plan"
      value={field.value}
      onValueChange={field.onChange}
      error={fieldState.error?.message}
    >
      <RadioItem value="free" label="Free" />
      <RadioItem value="pro" label="Pro" />
      <RadioItem value="enterprise" label="Enterprise" />
    </RadioGroup>
  )}
/>
```

## Tips & Gotchas

- **Select, Combobox, RadioGroup, and Slider use `onValueChange`**, not `onChange`. Always map the form library's change handler to `onValueChange`.

- **DatePicker uses `Date | undefined` with `onChange`.** Use a Controller-style
  adapter and call the form library's blur handler when the popover closes.

- **Checkbox and Switch use `onCheckedChange`**, not `onChange`. The callback receives a `boolean`, not an event.

- **InputOtp passes events via `inputProps`** — wrap the `onChange` handler inside it:
  ```tsx
  <InputOtp
    value={field.state.value}
    inputProps={{
      onChange: (e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value),
      onBlur: field.handleBlur,
    }}
    errorMessage={getFieldError(field)}
  />
  ```

- **TanStack Form errors are arrays**; React Hook Form errors are objects with a `.message` property. The `getFieldError` helper above normalizes TanStack's array format into a string.

- **Use `onBlur` for validation timing.** For Select and Combobox (which have no native blur), trigger it via `onOpenChange`:
  ```tsx
  onOpenChange={(open) => { if (!open) field.onBlur(); }}
  ```

- **Field + Input.** `Input` is a bare styled primitive. Wrap it in `Field` for `label`, `hideLabel`, `labelPlacement`, `optional`, `tooltip`, `description`, `error`, and adornments.

- **Slider's `onValueChange` receives `(value, event)`** — the value is `number | number[]`. Pass it directly to `field.handleChange` for TanStack Form, or `field.onChange` for React Hook Form.

- **Most form components support `name`; DatePicker currently does not.** Store
  its controlled `Date | undefined` value through your form library and serialize
  it explicitly when native form submission is required.

## Advanced: TanStack Form Composition Pattern

TanStack Form v1 supports a [composition pattern](https://tanstack.com/form/v1/docs/framework/react/guides/form-composition) that eliminates per-field wiring boilerplate. Instead of manually mapping `value`/`onChange`/`error` on every field, you create **pre-bound field components** that auto-connect via context.

This is the **recommended setup for teams using TanStack Form**. Copy this into your app (not shipped by FidoUI — keeps the library form-agnostic).

### 1. Create your app's form hook

```tsx
// src/lib/form.ts
import { createFormHookContexts, createFormHook } from '@tanstack/react-form'

// Import your pre-wired field components (see step 2)
import { TextField, TextareaField, SelectField, CheckboxField } from './form-fields'

const { fieldContext, formContext } = createFormHookContexts()

export { fieldContext, formContext }

export const { useAppForm } = createFormHook({
  fieldContext,
  formContext,
  fieldComponents: {
    TextField,
    TextareaField,
    SelectField,
    CheckboxField,
  },
})
```

### 2. Create pre-wired FidoUI field components

Each component uses `useFieldContext()` to auto-bind value, change handler, and errors:

```tsx
// src/lib/form-fields.tsx
import { useFieldContext } from '@tanstack/react-form'
import { Input } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/input'
import { Field } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/field'
import { Textarea } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/textarea'
import { Select, SelectItem } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/select'
import { Checkbox } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/checkbox'

function getFieldError(field: any) {
  if (!field.state.meta.isTouched || field.state.meta.isValid) return undefined
  return field.state.meta.errors.map((e: any) => typeof e === 'string' ? e : String(e)).join(', ')
}

export function TextField({ label, ...props }: { label: string } & Record<string, any>) {
  const field = useFieldContext<string>()
  return (
    <Field label={label} error={getFieldError(field)} {...props}>
      <Input
        name={field.name}
        value={field.state.value}
        onChange={(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value)}
        onBlur={field.handleBlur}
      />
    </Field>
  )
}

export function TextareaField({ label, ...props }: { label: string } & Record<string, any>) {
  const field = useFieldContext<string>()
  return (
    <Textarea
      label={label}
      name={field.name}
      value={field.state.value}
      onChange={(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value)}
      onBlur={field.handleBlur}
      error={getFieldError(field)}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

export function SelectField({ label, children, ...props }: { label: string; children: React.ReactNode } & Record<string, any>) {
  const field = useFieldContext<string>()
  return (
    <Select
      label={label}
      name={field.name}
      value={field.state.value}
      onValueChange={(v) => field.handleChange(v ?? '')}
      error={getFieldError(field)}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </Select>
  )
}

export function CheckboxField({ label, ...props }: { label: string } & Record<string, any>) {
  const field = useFieldContext<boolean>()
  return (
    <Checkbox
      label={label}
      name={field.name}
      checked={field.state.value}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => field.handleChange(!!checked)}
      error={getFieldError(field)}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}
```

### 3. Use in your forms — zero wiring

```tsx
import { useAppForm } from '@/lib/form'
import { SelectItem } from '@petscreeninginc/fido-ui/select'
import { z } from 'zod'

const schema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(2),
  email: z.string().email(),
  country: z.string().min(1, 'Required'),
  terms: z.literal(true, { errorMap: () => ({ message: 'Required' }) }),
})

function RegistrationForm() {
  const form = useAppForm({
    defaultValues: { name: '', email: '', country: '', terms: false as boolean },
    onSubmit: async ({ value }) => console.log(value),
  })

  return (
    <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); form.handleSubmit(); }}>
      {/* No manual value/onChange/error wiring needed! */}
      <form.AppField name="name" validators={{ onBlur: schema.shape.name }}>
        {(field) => <field.TextField label="Name" />}
      </form.AppField>

      <form.AppField name="email" validators={{ onBlur: schema.shape.email }}>
        {(field) => <field.TextField label="Email" />}
      </form.AppField>

      <form.AppField name="country" validators={{ onBlur: schema.shape.country }}>
        {(field) => (
          <field.SelectField label="Country">
            <SelectItem value="us">United States</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem value="ca">Canada</SelectItem>
          </field.SelectField>
        )}
      </form.AppField>

      <form.AppField name="terms" validators={{ onBlur: schema.shape.terms }}>
        {(field) => <field.CheckboxField label="I accept the terms" />}
      </form.AppField>

      <form.Subscribe selector={(state) => [state.canSubmit, state.isSubmitting]}>
        {([canSubmit, isSubmitting]) => (
          <Button color="primary" shade="dark" type="submit" disabled={!canSubmit || isSubmitting}>
            {isSubmitting ? 'Submitting...' : 'Submit'}
          </Button>
        )}
      </form.Subscribe>
    </form>
  )
}
```

This pattern gives you **type-safe forms with zero per-field boilerplate** while keeping FidoUI library-agnostic. Each team sets it up once in their app.
